title: Defined Benefit vs Defined Contribution (Exam Favorite)

blocks.content: In a Defined Benefit scheme, investment risk lies entirely with the employer, whereas in a Defined Contribution scheme, the employee bears the market risk.

items: NPS is a Defined Contribution scheme regulated by PFRDA, mandatory for central government employees joining on or after January 1, 2004.
Old Pension Scheme (OPS) is based on Defined Benefit, while the National Pension System (NPS) is based on Defined Contribution.
Exams frequently test risk allocation: DB places market risk on the Employer, while DC transfers market risk to the Employee.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Defined Benefit (DB) schemes promise a specified monthly payout upon retirement, calculated using a formula based on tenure and salary history.
Defined Contribution (DC) schemes fix the contribution amount, leaving the final retirement corpus dependent on accumulated investments and market returns.
In DB schemes, the employer bears the investment risk, whereas in DC schemes, the employee bears the market risk.
The National Pension System (NPS) is India's flagship Defined Contribution retirement scheme, regulated by PFRDA.
